title: Auto Accident — Client Intake
description: A personal injury lawyer conducts an initial intake with a client injured in a rear-end collision. Follows the evidence chain framework.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Thank you for coming in. Tell me in your own words what happened on the day of the accident.

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: It was the 14th of January, around 5:30 in the evening. I was stopped at a red light on Maple Avenue and a car just slammed into the back of me at full speed. I didn't even see it coming.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Were there any witnesses at the scene that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: Yes, a woman in the car next to me stopped and gave me her number. Her name is Sandra Okafor. And I think a cyclist stopped briefly but I never got their details.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Did the police attend? And was a report filed?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: Yes, two officers came. They filed a report on the spot. I have a copy at home — I can bring it.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Please do — that will be important. What about the other driver? Did they admit fault at the scene or say anything significant?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: He kept saying he didn't see the light change. He wasn't on his phone that I saw but he seemed distracted. He did say sorry twice before the police arrived.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Did you exchange insurance details with the other driver?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: Yes, I have his insurance card — it's State Farm. And I took photos of both vehicles, the damage, and his licence plate.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Excellent. Now let's talk about your injuries. What happened to you physically at the time of impact?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: My head snapped back hard. I had immediate pain in my neck and my right shoulder. My airbag didn't deploy because it was a rear hit so I hit the headrest.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Did you go to hospital that day?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: The ambulance took me to St. Catherine's ER. They did X-rays, said there were no fractures, and discharged me with painkillers. But the pain got worse over the following days.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Have you seen any other doctors or specialists since the ER visit?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: My GP referred me to a physiotherapist. I've had five sessions so far. I also saw an orthopaedic specialist last week who mentioned I might need an MRI.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Are you keeping records of all your treatment visits and expenses?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: Mostly yes. I have the ER bill and the physio invoices. I haven't got the specialist bill yet. I also had to take two weeks off work.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: That lost income is claimable. Do you have documentation from your employer confirming the time off?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: I have the sick leave form my manager signed. I wasn't paid during that time because I'd already used my sick days.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Have you been contacted by the other driver's insurance company at all?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: Yes, a claims adjuster from State Farm called me three days after the accident. They wanted to record a statement. I didn't say much — I told them I had a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: Good — never give a recorded statement without counsel. Did they make any settlement offers?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: They mentioned a figure of $4,500 but it felt very low given my medical bills alone are already over $3,000.

utterances.speaker: interviewer
utterances.text: You were right not to accept that. Is there any pre-existing injury or condition to the neck or shoulder that the other side might raise?

utterances.speaker: responder
utterances.text: I had some mild back stiffness about three years ago but nothing to do with my neck or shoulder. And I was completely fine before this accident.
